title: The Juice Spill Adventure
markdown:
A blustery afternoon. Sunshine painted zig-zag patterns on the floor. Ruby was having a snack with Dash the dog and Mr Clive, in a room so snug it felt like a hug. The kettle had just stopped singing. A clock ticked, unhurried.

Ruby had a tall glass of fizzy bubbly berry juice, shimmering like a tiny purple galaxy. The bubbles tickled her nose as she took a sip. Dash, a whirlwind of wagging fur, thumped his tail against the rug, a sure sign of pure doggy delight. Mr Clive, ever the calm one, was enjoying his tea, steam curling up like a wispy cloud.

WHOOPS. Ruby’s elbow nudged the tall glass. Before anyone could even say oh my whiskers, it tipped. A splash of bright purple juice, so vibrant it looked like a fallen splash of sunset, landed right on the lovely light rug. It spread out like a tiny purple puddle.

Ruby’s eyes widened — not with fear, with surprise. “Oopsie!” Dash let out a soft whimper, a sound of concern for his friends. Mr Clive’s eyes crinkled at the corners. “Well now. That’s quite a bit of juice that’s decided to go exploring. No worries at all. We need to clean it up quickly before it makes a stain, like a little purple footprint. Let’s see what we have that can help.”

He dashed off for a moment and returned with a small woven basket. Inside were different cloths, nestled together. A fluffy white one, so soft it felt like stroking a bunny’s ear. Next to it a smooth silky blue one that felt cool to the touch. And beside that, a scratchy green one that reminded Ruby of the prickly grass in the garden. “Let’s have a little experiment, shall we?”

Ruby watched with big curious eyes as Mr Clive carefully dabbed at the purple spill with the fluffy white cloth. Her head tilted. “Look, Dash! The juice is going into the cloth. It’s like the cloth is drinking it all up, like a big thirsty drink.” She watched as the white cloth grew heavier and darker, plump with the vibrant purple juice. Then Mr Clive picked up the smooth blue cloth. It soaked up some juice, yes, but it left a little damp patch behind. “Hmm. This cloth isn’t quite as thirsty.” Finally he tried the scratchy green cloth. Better than the blue, but the fluffy white one was still the champion juicer-drinker. “Wow!” Ruby giggled, a happy bubbly sound. “This white one is the thirstiest cloth ever.” She could see the juice disappearing into the soft fibres, leaving the rug beneath it almost completely dry.

“You’ve got it, Ruby. That fluffy white cloth is made of special material. It has lots of tiny spaces inside, like a whole bunch of little sponges all lined up. Those tiny spaces can hold lots of liquid. That special ability to soak up liquid is called absorbency. Some things soak up spills much better than others because of how they’re made.” He then used the fluffy white cloth to gently mop up the last little bit of juice, leaving the rug looking as good as new.

Dash, excited by all the discoveries and happy the rug was saved, nudged the fluffy cloth with his wet nose, as if to say clever cloth, well done. Ruby picked up the blue one and showed Dash how it soaked up a little puddle she made with her finger, then the green one. They giggled as they saw which one could drink more juice, turning it into a playful game.

Ruby sat back, the room snug again, the purple footprint gone. Different materials soak up liquids in different ways. The fluffy white cloth was a champion tidier-upper because it was super absorbent, filled with tiny spaces ready to hold liquid. She wondered what else might be thirsty, or not thirsty at all, and Dash thumped his tail as if he wondered too.
characters: Ruby (a shape spotter), Dash (a dog), Clive (a gardener)
